- SNTRU Prime and NTRU LPRime decapsulation compared the received ciphertext with the re-encrypted one in constant time, but then turned the result into the implicit-rejection mask with a conditional, a branch on whether the ciphertext was valid. The mask is now derived arithmetically from the accumulated difference, as the reference implementation does.

- SNTRU Prime and NTRU LPRime sign-extended the last byte of a public key or ciphertext encoding when its final value spans two bytes, which happens for most parameter sets, so an encoding with that byte at 0x80 or above decoded to different values than the reference implementation's. Only non-canonical encodings were affected, since a valid one's last byte is below 0x40: a malformed public key was encapsulated against a different polynomial than the reference would use, and a malformed ciphertext is rejected either way.

- SNTRU Prime and NTRU LPRime decapsulation derived the implicit-rejection secret for an invalid ciphertext from the ciphertext it re-encrypted from the decrypted message, where the NTRU Prime specification and reference implementation hash the ciphertext received, and NTRU LPRime also hashed it under the prefix used for a valid ciphertext. The re-encryption depends only on the decrypted message, so two invalid ciphertexts that decrypted to the same message gave the same secret - for example a valid ciphertext with its confirmation hash changed in two different ways - and anyone able to compare decapsulation results under one key could tell whether two chosen ciphertexts decrypt to the same message: the plaintext-checking oracle implicit rejection exists to deny. NTRU LPRime before 1.85 put the received rounded polynomial and T in the hash, which limited the collisions to ciphertexts differing only in the confirmation hash. The rejection secret now depends only on rho and the received ciphertext, and secrets for valid ciphertexts are unchanged. Keys used for a single decapsulation, as in SSH's sntrup761x25519-sha512 key exchange, are not exposed.

+- NTRU+ decapsulation never reported a rejected ciphertext. The NTRU+ reference implementation rejects explicitly, returning failure with a zeroed secret, and NTRUPlusKEMExtractor discarded the failure and returned the secret as a shared key, so every invalid ciphertext gave the same all-zero secret, which anyone can compute. Worse, when the message decoding check failed, a sign error in its port of the reference's unsigned failure flag left the real secret derived from the decrypted message in place with only the low bit of each byte cleared. Either way anyone able to submit ciphertexts to a key could tell from the result whether, and to what, a chosen ciphertext decrypts. extractSecret() now throws IllegalArgumentException for a rejected ciphertext, which the BCPQC provider reports as a DecapsulateException from javax.crypto.KEM and an InvalidKeyException from Cipher.unwrap(). Ciphertexts and public keys with a coefficient of q or more are now also refused as non-canonical encodings, as the reference implementation does. Secrets for valid ciphertexts are unchanged.

- The BC provider registered no key info converter for the NTRU LPRime, Streamlined NTRU Prime and NTRU+ OIDs, although core's key factories handle all of them, so BouncyCastleProvider.getPublicKey() and getPrivateKey() returned null for such a SubjectPublicKeyInfo or PrivateKeyInfo, and their keys and certificates could not be decoded through the standard provider's CertificateFactory or KeyFactory, only through BCPQC. The twelve NTRU Prime and three NTRU+ parameter-set OIDs are now bridged in loadPQCKeys(), as the other BCPQC KEMs already were (github PR #2438).

- PGPLiteralData.getFileName() and LiteralDataPacket.getFileName() threw an IllegalArgumentException for a file name that was not valid UTF-8, which the file name need not be and which a damaged ciphertext produces, since the literal data header is read before any integrity check. The high-level OpenPGPMessageProcessor reads the file name for every message, so such a message could not be read through it at all, and a damaged one failed with this unchecked exception instead of the integrity check. A malformed sequence in the file name is now decoded as U+FFFD, as it now is in SignerUserID.getID(); valid names decode exactly as before, and getRawFileName() and getRawID() still return the exact bytes (github #2549).

- The BC provider's EC services (signatures, key agreement, IES and the SM2, GOST and DSTU variants) now report an EC key whose domain parameters do not form a valid curve with InvalidKeyException, carrying the reason as its cause, where a public key from another provider, or a key implementing BC's own ECPublicKey or ECPrivateKey interface, let an IllegalArgumentException escape from init. A BC-interface key with implicitlyCA parameters when none are configured gave a NullPointerException and now also gets InvalidKeyException. A BC-interface public key with no parameters now uses the configured implicitlyCA parameters, as the private key already did, while a key from another provider with no parameters is refused with "has no domain parameters", the JCA having no implicitlyCA. A private key from another provider with invalid parameters is reported as invalid, keeping the "parameters are not accessible (a hardware-backed key?)" message for keys whose accessors fail.
